A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Implicit-ARAP work. All pages, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v1's appendices. Much appendix material is incorporated into v2's main text, allowing retained content and omissions to be distinguished.

before.justification: V1 reports original mesh and neural-field deformation experiments, numerical comparisons, runtime measurements and patch sensitivity analyses in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds DeFAUST evaluations and a qualitative loss ablation, including Tables 3–4 and Figures 11 and 13.

M1.justification: The patch construction and deformation architectures are retained. The written SDF-fitting Eikonal loss changes from E||grad f-1|| to E(||grad f||-1)^2, a localized correction to the reported objective. The PDFs do not establish that the implementation changed; most expanded architecture details already appeared in v1 Appendix B.

E1.justification: V2 adds DeFAUST human-body deformation evaluations for both pipelines, extending coverage beyond v1's handcrafted Thingi10k and Stanford shape experiments. The original collection is retained under the new name TFD; that renaming itself does not add coverage.

E2.justification: ARAP, Elastic, SR-ARAP and NFGP remain the comparators in the corresponding mesh and neural-field experiments, and Marching Cubes remains the meshing comparator. DeFAUST uses the same baseline set. SShaDe is cited for the dataset but is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: V2 adds DeFAUST-specific settings: 2000 deformation steps, ARAP weight 10000 and patch radius 0.01, versus TFD's 1000 steps, weight 10 and radius 0.03. Its TFD tables explicitly exclude octopus, and patch scaling is reported over TFD instead of Stanford dragon alone. Existing evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 13 adds a controlled comparison of the full method, zero-level-only patches and handle loss without ARAP regularization. Figure 15 broadens the existing radius/density analysis to TFD averages. Earlier discretization, invertibility, sampling-distribution and handle-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The reconstruction plots retain mean-to-maximum spatial error shading, rather than statistical uncertainty estimates. Dataset averaging in v2 does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 Tables 3–4 add DeFAUST results, including mesh volume errors of 0.99% for Ours and 15.02% for NFGP, and Figure 15 changes the sensitivity curves. V1's all-case and octopus-specific numerical summaries are removed. Retained TFD values match earlier Subset or Drop highest entries, rather than demonstrating new performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the Eikonal definition from v1 Appendix B, Eq. (15), to squared gradient-norm deviation in Eq. (12). It also introduces the inline relation x'=d_phi(x) in Section 3.2, inconsistent with its retained inverse-field equation (7). No new theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: local patch meshing, two ARAP deformation pipelines, and claims of efficiency, quality, robustness and scalability. The new experiments support these existing claims without substantially redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 Section 5.1 qualifies the runtime advantage: the method is faster on TFD but slower than explicit methods on DeFAUST on average, attributed to lower vertex counts. It emphasizes SDF fitting as a bottleneck and interprets the new ablation as evidence for ARAP and multi-level regularization. Existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies DeFAUST settings but omits v1's sampling pseudocode, parallelization explanation and individual Thingiverse links. Architecture and hardware details are largely relocated. Code availability changes from future to present tense, although both PDFs retain the same placeholder code URL.

R1.justification: V2 adds FAUST and SShaDe references and a short discussion of text-guided neural and Gaussian-based editing, citing works including CLIP-NeRF, GaussianEditor and GSEdit. NFGP remains the closest prior method; the inefficiency criticism is narrowed from earlier solutions collectively to NFGP specifically.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the document by incorporating architecture, shape-model, patch-discretization and hardware material from the appendices into the main methods and experiments sections. It adds a Shape model subsection, restructures experimental discussion and revises explanatory prose throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adds DeFAUST and ablation figures, restructures result tables into TFD/DeFAUST blocks with value highlighting, and redraws sensitivity plots. Architecture and sampling figures move into the main text, while retained comparison figures are rearranged. V1's sampling pseudocode display and mesh-link table disappear.

improvement.justification: The DeFAUST comparisons, direct loss ablation and explicit runtime qualification make the empirical evidence broader and more informative. Consolidated technical material also improves readability. However, v2 removes inclusive and octopus-specific numerical summaries and some reproducibility details, and introduces an inverse-map explanation error. These tradeoffs limit the overall gain.
